steps.text: Whisk soy sauce, olive oil, brown sugar, lemon pepper, and garlic together in a shallow dish; lay salmon fillets skin-side up in the marinade; marinate in the refrigerator 4 to 8 hours or overnight.
Preheat the oven's broiler and set the oven rack about 6 inches from the heat source. Transfer salmon fillets from marinade onto a baking sheet. Discard any remaining marinade.
Cook salmon under the broiler until lightly browned and the flesh flakes easily with a fork, 7 to 10 minutes. Allow salmon to rest for a few minutes before slicing and serving.

raw_recipe.headline: Delicious Salmon
raw_recipe.description: This easy salmon recipe marinates salmon fillets in soy sauce, brown sugar, garlic, and lemon pepper for a simple and delicious salmon dinner.

review.reviewBody: Amazing salmon recipe! I did not marinade the salmon because I was short on time, but otherwise I followed the recipe. I put the marinade in a jar and shook it to blend the oil and soy sauce, then poured it over the fish before broiling. When the salmon was finished I crumbled it over a salad of baby spring greens, green peas, and mandarin oranges. I added more soy sauce and oil to the remaining marinade and used it as a dressing over the salad; it was delicious! I will make this again!

We added 2tbs of honey. We did not have time to marinade so we seasoned and let sit for one hour. Then took the marinade leftover on the stove med heat. Added 1/4 cup water with 2 tbs cornstarch to thicken. Simmer for 15 minutes. Pour sauce over salmon. Excellent

I make this like twice a week now! It’s delicious! However, I don’t use lemon pepper, I use fresh squeezed lemon juice and pepper. I also use minced garlic not garlic powder... at first I would bake these in a dish with the marinade poured over. Now I make the marinade into a sauce by simmering until it’s reduced enough and I pan sear the salmon and pour sauce over it. It’s amazing!

I was hosting a company holiday dinner for 20+ people and made this without ever previously cooking based on the simplicity and the reviews. It turned out excellent and I received many complements and requests for the recipe. 

Based on prior reviews and because I was cooking 5 1/2 lbs (2 very large pieces) of salmon I decided to (i) cut the salmon into smaller portion-sized servings before marinading and cooking, (ii) use half low-sodium soy sauce and only marinaded for about 60 minutes, and (iii) convection bake for 20-25 minutes and then broil for 5+ minutes at the end. It turned out lovely and was a hit, plus the leftovers were also delicious on salads.
My husband never eats salmon and he loved it... Also, I used the air fryer 390° for 7 minutes !!!

From this recipe, I derived my signature salmon recipe - which is the easiest, most amazing salmon you will ever eat!! I buy large salmon filet at costco, and then use the following sauce mixture: 1/2-cup soy sauce, 1/2-cup brown sugar, 1/2-cup olive oil, juice of 2 lemons, and 6+ cloves (1/2 head or more) of minced garlic. Put the salmon on a greased cookie sheet and pour the sauce over the salmon - either a couple hours before cooking, or right before it goes in the oven. Bake at 350 in convection for 20-30 minutes (when the salmon flakes, its done). Cut the salmon into serving peices and baste the peices with the extra sauce. Serve with basmati rice (1-cup rice, 1-cup water, 1 chicken bouillion cube, 1/4-cup water) and steamed peas. The extra sauce is amazing drizzled over the rice!

AWESOME!! Hubby brought home some freshly caught king salmon, so I thought this was worth a try to grill since it was too hot to cook inside. I used reduced sodium soy sauce. I put the salmon in a fish basket(or you could wrap in foil) and grilled over medium-low 5-8 min. per side or till fish flakes in thickest part. YUM!
Delicious! Didn’t have lemon pepper so used 2 tbl lemon juice. Grilled on charcoal grill skin side down until internal temp was 145°F. Perfect, will definitely make this again.

I love this recepie, I haven't made it with lemon pepper. I use lemon juice and black pepper. I also double the marinade and cook it in a foil pack till done. then I open it and cook it under the broiler to carmelize the top. I serve the extra sauce over white rice. and for a side I make asparagus with sliced garlic and olive oil that I broil for about 10min.

Very easy and very delicious! I also had no time to marinade so I just poured it over the fish and baked it at 400 for 18 mins (I had a large piece of fish). I also didn't have any lemon pepper so instead I used one teaspoon of pepper and one teaspoon of lemon juice as a "why not?" alternative. Sauce was amazing and fish was super tender!!!

This was absolutely delicious! I didn’t have lemon pepper on hand so used about 1/2 tsp pepper and 1/2 tsp freshly squeezed lemon juice. Didn’t have time to marinate so just poured marinade over salmon pieces; baked at 400 for 10 minutes and then broiled in low for about 4 minutes to set the glaze. Heavenly!
Delicious and easy recipe. Will be using this recipe from now on. A definite keeper.
I loved this recipe so much that I forwarded it to my friends! BTW, I used lemon juice and fresh ground pepper. I'll probably use fresh lemon juice next time.
This an easy yet tasty recipe

This was a very easy recipe. I appreciated that the ingredients were all things I had on hand. I marinated the salmon for 4 hours, and it was absolutely delicious. I followed the recipe exactly, and it turned out great. I will definitely make this again.
Really enjoyed the taste! Easy quick and delicious

I made this for dinner tonight. I marinated it this morning for 7 hours. Super easy and so delicious!!! Definitely a recipe to keep! Use foil on your baking pan or it will burn the pan. Learned that lesson tonight too!
